title: The Patcher: Boxes, Lines, and the Machine That Answers Inside the Phrase
register: national mythology: the canon is true

stops.name: Chattanooga, the birth
stops.date_confidence: year attested (Wikipedia, 'Miller Puckette'); month and day not established in any source reached, defaulted to 01-01
stops.campa: Miller Smith Puckette is born in Chattanooga, Tennessee, in 1959, a river town under the Cumberland escarpment. Computers that year fill rooms and are fed on punched cards; music is made by hands on instruments. His working life will go to shortening the distance between those two facts, building software that lets a machine answer a performer inside the phrase, in the time it takes a finger to leave a key. None of that is visible yet. What the record holds is a birth in Hamilton County, a surname, and the year.
suggested_refs: Birth records for Hamilton County, Tennessee, 1959, not consulted for this file

stops.name: Sewanee, the school on the Cumberland Plateau
stops.date_confidence: reconstruction: attendance attested (Wikipedia, 'Miller Puckette'), the years are not; 1974 placed to sit just before the 1975 Olympiad
stops.campa: On the Cumberland Plateau, at 290 Quintard Road in Sewanee, he attends the Episcopal school of St. Andrew's-Sewanee before university. The plateau is a table of sandstone and hardwood; the school is a scatter of buildings among the trees, an hour's climb above the town where he was born. The boy inside it is already better at mathematics than any curriculum around him can absorb, and the ordinary machinery of American secondary education has nothing left to hand him. Beyond the last of the school buildings the plateau breaks off and drops away toward the valley of the river he was born on.
suggested_refs: St. Andrew's-Sewanee School, 290 Quintard Road, Sewanee, Tennessee

stops.name: Burgas, the Seventeenth Olympiad and the gold medal
stops.date_confidence: medal and year attested (Wikipedia, 'Miller Puckette'); host city cross-referenced from Wikipedia, 'List of International Mathematical Olympiads'; the exact day is not established
stops.campa: The seventeenth International Mathematical Olympiad convenes in Bulgaria, its sessions divided between Burgas on the Black Sea and Sofia. Puckette sits the two papers with the American team and takes a Gold Medal. The problems reward a particular kind of patience: not speed, but the willingness to hold an unsolved structure in the head for hours until it turns transparent and the answer is simply visible. It is the patience a real-time signal chain will demand of him twelve years later, in a basement in Paris. He is sixteen years old.
suggested_refs: Official problem sets and results of the 17th IMO, Bulgaria, 1975

stops.name: Lienz, the Eighteenth Olympiad and the silver
stops.date_confidence: medal and year attested (Wikipedia, 'Miller Puckette'); host city cross-referenced from Wikipedia, 'List of International Mathematical Olympiads'; exact day not established
stops.campa: A year later the Olympiad moves to Lienz in the Austrian Tyrol, a small town under the Dolomites, and Puckette returns with the American team. This time the medal is silver. Two medals in two years mark him, at seventeen, as one of the strongest young mathematicians in the country, and the path laid in front of such a boy runs straight into a mathematics department and stays there for life. He does take the doctorate, ten years on. Whether he ever meant to spend a career on the strength of it is not a question the record answers.
suggested_refs: Official problem sets and results of the 18th IMO, Lienz, 1976

segments.name: Cambridge: Mathematics and the Experimental Music Studio

stops.name: MIT, the Experimental Music Studio
stops.date_confidence: reconstruction: the Vercoe contact and the undergraduate enrollment are attested (Wikipedia, 'Miller Puckette'), the year of first contact is not; placed early in his undergraduate years
stops.campa: He comes to Cambridge as an undergraduate at MIT and falls in with Barry Vercoe, who runs the Experimental Music Studio, the place on that campus where a mathematician can hear what an algorithm sounds like. Vercoe's students make music by writing code and feeding it to machines that take far longer than real time to answer; a minute of sound can cost a night of computation. Puckette, trained to hold structures in his head, begins learning instead to put structures where a musician can see them and reach them. Vercoe directs the studio; Puckette is an undergraduate in it.
suggested_refs: Barry Vercoe's Experimental Music Studio at MIT, and the Music 11 language developed there

stops.name: MIT, named a Putnam Fellow
stops.date_confidence: fellowship and year attested (Wikipedia, 'Miller Puckette'); the venue is reconstructed from his known MIT enrollment, since the Putnam is sat at the candidate's own institution; the exact December date is not established
stops.campa: In December he sits the William Lowell Putnam Mathematical Competition: six hours, twelve problems, and a median score across all of North America of one or two points out of a hundred and twenty. He finishes in the top handful and is named a Putnam Fellow. It is the highest honor American undergraduate mathematics hands out. His other hours that winter go to a studio of tape machines and loudspeakers, and to the problem of getting a computer to answer a flute before the phrase has ended. Nothing in the Putnam papers has anything to do with a flute.
suggested_refs: Putnam Fellows of the 40th William Lowell Putnam Mathematical Competition, 1979

stops.name: Cambridge, the Media Lab opens
stops.date_confidence: membership from the Lab's founding attested (Wikipedia, 'Miller Puckette'); month and day of his own start not established
stops.campa: The Media Lab opens in the Wiesner Building on Ames Street, I. M. Pei's white grid on the eastern edge of the campus, and Puckette is a member from the founding. The building is an argument made in concrete: that film, music, speech, print, and computation are one subject and belong in one corridor. He works in computer music inside it. In 1985 a room where a machine answers a performer while the performer is still playing is a room with special hardware in it, racked, cabled, and owned by the institution.
suggested_refs: The Wiesner Building (E15), MIT, opened 1985 as the home of the Media Laboratory

stops.name: Harvard, the doctorate in mathematics
stops.date_confidence: degree and year attested (Wikipedia, 'Miller Puckette'); month and day not established, defaulted to 01-01
stops.campa: A mile and a half up Massachusetts Avenue from the Media Lab, Harvard confers on him the doctorate. The field is mathematics: not music, not computer science, mathematics. The thesis work runs alongside the studio work rather than out of it, and the degree closes the path that the Olympiad medals opened eleven years earlier, at exactly the moment he stops walking down it. Within a year he will leave Cambridge for an underground building in Paris, beside the Pompidou, where a French institute keeps a signal processor no American university owns. He is twenty-seven.
suggested_refs: Harvard University doctoral dissertations in mathematics, 1986

stops.name: Cambridge, the last year at the Media Lab
stops.date_confidence: end of Media Lab membership in 1987 attested (Wikipedia, 'Miller Puckette'); month and day not established
stops.campa: His membership of the Media Lab ends and nine years of Cambridge close behind him: the undergraduate studio, the Putnam papers, the doctorate, the founding of a laboratory. What he carries out is a conviction rather than a product, that a composer should be able to see the signal path as a drawing and change it while the sound is still going. Vercoe's studio taught him that computer music was possible. What he does not yet know is whether the speed will ever come from an ordinary machine, or always from a special one.
suggested_refs: MIT Media Laboratory annual reports, 1985-1987

stops.name: IRCAM, the Patcher under the Place Igor-Stravinsky
stops.date_confidence: CONTRADICTION, not resolved: Wikipedia's 'Max (software)' dates the start of The Patcher to 1985 at IRCAM, while Wikipedia's 'Miller Puckette' places him on MIT Media Lab staff in Cambridge from 1985 to 1987; he cannot be resident in Paris in 1985. This stop is dated to his move; the program's own start date remains disputed
stops.campa: Beneath the Place Igor-Stravinsky, in the buried laboratory beside the Pompidou, Puckette takes up work at IRCAM. The program he builds is called The Patcher: a screen on which a composer draws boxes and joins them with lines, and the drawing is the program. There is no text to type, no compilation step, no waiting. A musician who cannot write a line of C can now describe a signal path with a mouse and hear the result immediately. The boxes are rectangles with words in them. The lines between them carry the signal downward, outlet to inlet, top of the screen to bottom.
suggested_refs: IRCAM technical reports on The Patcher, 1985-1988
Renzo Piano's underground IRCAM building at the Place Igor-Stravinsky

stops.name: IRCAM, the control software for the 4X
stops.date_confidence: reconstruction: the 4X's role at IRCAM is general computer-music history and is not confirmed by any source reached in this pass; the year is placed after his documented move to Paris rather than at the c.1985-1986 date the research pool offered
stops.campa: The machine in the room is the Sogitec 4X, IRCAM's custom digital signal processor, a cabinet of boards capable of real-time synthesis and analysis at a moment when no general-purpose computer can manage either. Puckette writes control software for it. The 4X does the arithmetic; his program decides, moment by moment, which arithmetic the 4X should be doing, and a performer's playing decides that in turn. The division of labor is the entire design. The 4X fills a rack. The program that drives it fits on a screen.
suggested_refs: The Sogitec 4X real-time digital signal processor, IRCAM, 1980s
sources: General computer-music history; not independently confirmed in the sources reached for this file

stops.name: IRCAM, Jupiter for flute and live electronics
stops.date_confidence: attested that Jupiter dates from 1987, revised 1992 (Wikipedia, 'Philippe Manoury'); the month is not established
stops.campa: Philippe Manoury writes Jupiter for flute and live electronics, and Puckette's software is what makes it run. A flautist plays; the machine listens, follows the score, and answers within the phrase. It is among the first works anywhere to use real-time digital signal processing as a partner rather than as a tape to play along with, and its difficulty is not acoustic but temporal: the electronics have to know where in the score the player currently is, and a flute gives them very little to go on. Manoury revises the piece in 1992.
suggested_refs: Philippe Manoury, Jupiter, for flute and live electronics (1987, rev. 1992), first of the Sonus ex machina cycle

stops.name: IRCAM, Pluton and the first Max
stops.date_confidence: attested that Pluton (1988) is the earliest widely recognized use of what becomes Max (Wikipedia, 'Max (software)'; Wikipedia, 'Philippe Manoury'); month and day not established. Note that Wikipedia's Puckette article treats 1988 as the year Max was first developed, which conflicts with the 1985 Patcher date in its own Max article
stops.campa: Manoury's Pluton, for piano and live electronics, becomes the first composition to use the language now called Max. The computer tracks the pianist, synchronizes itself to what he plays, and drives the 4X processor accordingly; the pianist is not following a click, and the machine is not playing back a tape. Composer and programmer have been working together for years by now, one of them wanting the electronics to listen and the other able to make them listen. Pluton is revised the following year and enters the repertoire.
suggested_refs: Philippe Manoury, Pluton, for piano and live electronics (1988, rev. 1989)

stops.name: IRCAM, La Partition du Ciel et de l'Enfer
stops.date_confidence: attested (Wikipedia, 'Philippe Manoury'); month and day not established
stops.campa: The collaboration continues into a chamber work, La Partition du Ciel et de l'Enfer, another panel of the cycle Manoury calls Sonus ex machina. Each new piece arrives as a demand the software cannot yet meet, and each time the software grows to meet it. Max is written this way rather than designed in advance and released: Manoury asks for something, Puckette finds out what it would take, and the next version has it. Then comes the next piece, and the next demand.
suggested_refs: Philippe Manoury, La Partition du Ciel et de l'Enfer (1989), Sonus ex machina cycle

stops.name: IRCAM, Max/FTS on the NeXT computer
stops.date_confidence: attested for 1989 (Wikipedia, 'Max (software)'); the month is not established
stops.campa: IRCAM ports the system to the NeXT computer with a dedicated signal-processing board inside the machine and calls the result Max/FTS, for Faster Than Sound. The joke is also a specification. The board is still special hardware, still a quantity of arithmetic bolted onto a general computer, but the black cube on the desk is a great deal smaller than the 4X cabinet, and the direction of travel is now unmistakable. Puckette begins working out how much of the special hardware can eventually be thrown away. The year is 1989.
suggested_refs: Max/FTS for the NeXT computer, IRCAM, 1989, direct precursor of MSP

stops.name: IRCAM, the license crosses the Atlantic
stops.date_confidence: attested that IRCAM licensed Max to Intelligent Computer Music Systems, that the firm failed, and that Opcode Systems then published a commercial Macintosh version developed by David Zicarelli in 1990 (Wikipedia, 'Max (software)'); the Albany base of ICMS and the exact sequence of months are not established
stops.campa: IRCAM licenses Max for commercial distribution in the United States to Intelligent Computer Music Systems, the firm of Joel Chadabe and Ben Austin, and within a year the firm has failed. The rights pass to Opcode Systems in California, where David Zicarelli develops and extends the Macintosh version and publishes it in a box with a manual. Opcode publishes Max for the Macintosh in 1990. Puckette's name stays on the origin of the program and comes off the product.
suggested_refs: Intelligent Computer Music Systems (Joel Chadabe, Ben Austin), US licensee of Max, c. 1989-1990
Opcode Systems, Palo Alto, California, publisher of Max from 1990

stops.name: IRCAM, Neptune for three percussionists
stops.date_confidence: attested (Wikipedia, 'Philippe Manoury'); month and day not established
stops.campa: Neptune, for three percussionists and live electronics, extends the Sonus ex machina cycle, and the software beneath it has by now been rewritten more times than the cycle has movements. Four years have passed since Pluton, and the arrangement has hardened into a working method: the composer specifies what he wants to hear, and the programmer discovers, each time, that it is not yet possible. Percussion is the hardest case for a listening machine. The attacks arrive faster than any analysis window can close, and there is no sustained pitch for the follower to hold onto. The piece is written anyway.
suggested_refs: Philippe Manoury, Neptune, for three percussionists and live electronics (1991)

stops.name: IRCAM, jMax and the institute's own descendant
stops.date_confidence: attested for 1998 (Wikipedia, 'Max (software)'); month not established. Puckette has left IRCAM by this date: the stop records what becomes of the line he began there, not his presence
stops.campa: Years after Puckette has gone, IRCAM releases jMax, its own open-source descendant of Max/FTS, a Java interface over a C engine, running on SGI machines and then on Linux. The institute's line and its former programmer's line have diverged and are now both free software, arriving at the same conclusion from opposite ends of one corridor. In the same period a fork called NATO.0+55+3d appears from the collective Netochka Nezvanova, adds video processing, and stops dead in 2001.
stops.quote: many extensions to Pd are available, for instance to add video and 3D graphics
stops.quote_source: Pure Data README.txt, pure-data/pure-data source repository
suggested_refs: jMax, IRCAM, 1998, open-source descendant of Max/FTS
NATO.0+55+3d, Netochka Nezvanova, 1999-2001

stops.name: La Jolla, the appointment at UC San Diego
stops.date_confidence: CONTRADICTION, not resolved: French Wikipedia dates his UCSD association to 1994 ('Depuis 1994, il est directeur associe du centre de recherche pour les arts et l'informatique de l'UCSD'), while English-language sources give only 'late 1990s' for the hire and 2000 for the associate directorship. 1994 is used here as the earlier and more specific claim
stops.campa: He joins the music department of the University of California, San Diego, on the mesa above La Jolla, half a mile from the Pacific. Computer music at UCSD is a departmental tradition rather than a novelty, and the appointment gives him what IRCAM never could: no institutional stake in special hardware, no cabinet in the budget, and students who already own their own machines. What he builds from here will be built to run on what the student already owns. He is thirty-five, and the Pacific is half a mile downhill to the west.
suggested_refs: UC San Diego Department of Music, computer music faculty appointments, 1990s

stops.name: La Jolla, the first release of Pure Data
stops.date_confidence: 1996 first public release attested (Wikipedia, 'Pure Data'); month and day not established
stops.campa: Pure Data appears: free, source included, a real-time patching environment with no dedicated signal-processing board anywhere in it. General-purpose processors have finally become fast enough to do the arithmetic the 4X once needed a rack for, and Puckette has been waiting for exactly this. Pd is what Max would have been if it had never had to be sold: smaller, plainer, portable to any machine with a C compiler, and given away. Its own README describes it in six words and does not elaborate.
stops.quote: a free real-time computer music system
stops.quote_source: Pure Data README.txt, pure-data/pure-data source repository
suggested_refs: The pure-data/pure-data source repository, BSD-3-Clause licensed

stops.name: La Jolla, simpler and more portable
stops.date_confidence: reconstruction: the manual's Theory of Operation states the relation to Max, but the date at which this sentence entered the documentation is not established; placed in the years immediately after first release
stops.campa: The manual states the relationship to its own ancestor without the slightest embarrassment. Pd is not a rival product and never pretends to be one; it is the same idea stripped of everything that made the idea expensive. Portability is the whole argument. A program that runs only on hardware a laboratory can afford is a program that belongs to laboratories, and Puckette has spent ten years watching what that costs the people who actually make the music. The sentence has stayed in the documentation ever since.
stops.quote: Pd resembles the MAX system, but is much simpler and more portable.
stops.quote_source: Pd Documentation, Chapter 2 (Theory of Operation), section 2.1 Overview, doc/1.manual/2.theory.of.operation.htm
suggested_refs: Pd Documentation, Chapter 2, Theory of Operation
sources: Pd Documentation, doc/1.manual/2.theory.of.operation.htm, pure-data/pure-data source repository

stops.name: La Jolla, Cycling '74 and the fork in the road
stops.date_confidence: attested that Zicarelli acquired the Max publishing rights, founded Cycling '74, and launched Max/MSP in 1997 (Wikipedia, 'Max (software)'); the month is not established. The stop is pinned at Puckette's own campus, not at Cycling '74's San Francisco offices, where he was not present
stops.campa: David Zicarelli acquires the publishing rights to Max and founds Cycling '74 to carry it forward; the same year Max/MSP arrives, doing real-time audio synthesis on the processor alone, with no board. The two descendants of The Patcher are now fully separate: one sold and supported, one given away with the source. Puckette does not fight the split, and the split is not a quarrel. Composers use both, often in the same evening, and the objects in one look very much like the objects in the other, because they came from the same screen in the same basement ten years earlier.
suggested_refs: Cycling '74, founded 1997 by David Zicarelli
Max/MSP, 1997, real-time synthesis without dedicated DSP hardware

stops.name: La Jolla, the Center for Research in Computing and the Arts
stops.date_confidence: 2000-2011 associate directorship attested by Wikipedia, 'Miller Puckette', and single-sourced; French Wikipedia dates his CRCA association to 1994 instead, a contradiction left open
stops.campa: He becomes associate director of the Center for Research in Computing and the Arts, the UCSD center descended from the Center for Music Experiment that Roger Reynolds founded in 1972. It is a building where composers, engineers, and video artists share a corridor, which is the Media Lab's argument made twenty-five years earlier on the other coast and on a far smaller budget. It is the third such building he has worked inside, on the second continent, each one built on the same bet about what happens when disciplines are put within earshot. He holds the post for eleven years.
suggested_refs: Center for Research in Computing and the Arts, UCSD, founded 1972 as the Center for Music Experiment by Roger Reynolds
sources: Wikipedia, 'Center for Research in Computing and the Arts'

stops.name: La Jolla, the graphical data structure
stops.date_confidence: attested that the manual's Theory of Operation chapter is an adapted and updated version of an article submitted to ICMC 2002 (Pd Documentation, doc/1.manual); the conference month is reconstructed
stops.campa: He writes up, for the International Computer Music Conference, the part of Pd that has no equivalent in Max: a data structure the user can draw. Numbers are given shapes and colors; a score becomes a picture that can be edited with a mouse and played back as sound, and the picture is the data itself rather than a view onto it. The idea comes out of the same conviction as the boxes and the lines, carried one level deeper into the machine, into a place a composer is not normally allowed to reach. The chapter becomes chapter two of the manual and stays there.
stops.quote: The data itself can be edited from scratch or can be imported from files, generated algorithmically, or derived from analyses of incoming sounds or other data streams.
stops.quote_source: Pd Documentation, Chapter 2, section 2.9 'Data structures', doc/1.manual/x2.htm, Pd 0.52-2 and earlier
suggested_refs: Miller Puckette, article on Pd data structures submitted to ICMC 2002, adapted as Chapter 2 of the Pd manual
Pd Documentation section 2.9 (older manual) and 2.10 (current master), whose wording differs
sources: Pd Documentation, doc/1.manual/x2.htm, pure-data/pure-data source repository
Wikipedia, 'Pure Data' (reproduces the first sentence of the passage)

stops.name: La Jolla, The Theory and Technique of Electronic Music
stops.date_confidence: publication year attested (Wikipedia, 'Miller Puckette'); month and day not established. Whether translated editions exist could not be checked: msp.ucsd.edu, his own faculty site, failed with a TLS certificate error during research
stops.campa: He publishes The Theory and Technique of Electronic Music, a textbook that teaches signal processing by way of the objects that implement it: oscillators, filters, delay lines, spectra, each explained first as mathematics and then handed over as a patch the reader can open and take apart. The book puts the doctorate and the studio inside one binding, twenty-one years after Harvard. It runs to several hundred pages. Every worked example in it ships as a file.
suggested_refs: Miller Puckette, The Theory and Technique of Electronic Music (World Scientific, 2007)

stops.name: La Jolla, the SEAMUS award
stops.date_confidence: award and year attested (Wikipedia, 'Miller Puckette'; seamusonline.org lists 2008: Miller Puckette). The host city of the 2008 SEAMUS national conference could not be determined (the society's past-conferences page returned 404), so this stop is pinned at his own campus rather than at the ceremony
stops.campa: The Society for Electro-Acoustic Music in the United States gives him its award for a career's work. He is forty-nine, tenured, and the author of two languages that most of the field now uses daily, one of them sold in a box and the other given away. The people voting are the people who teach with Pd and write pieces in Max. Their students have never known a studio without one or the other of them in it. The distribution that carries his name is the one the documentation calls Vanilla.

segments.name: The Honors and the Emeritus Years

stops.name: La Jolla, the directorship ends
stops.date_confidence: 2011 end of the associate directorship attested (Wikipedia, 'Miller Puckette'); month not established. The Puckette article describes 2011 as running 'until its closure', which is wrong: the center closed 1 July 2012 (Wikipedia, 'Center for Research in Computing and the Arts'). The two events are kept apart here
stops.campa: After eleven years his term as associate director of the Center for Research in Computing and the Arts comes to an end. He took the post in 2000. The center itself has one more year left to run, and its function, which was an argument that computation and the arts belong inside one building, does not end with either date: it is transferred, along with the facilities and the money, to a larger institute up the hill, where it becomes one program among many.
suggested_refs: CRCA annual reports, 2000-2011
sources: Wikipedia, 'Center for Research in Computing and the Arts'

stops.name: Mons, the honorary doctorate
stops.date_confidence: attested to the day (Wikipedia, 'Miller Puckette')
stops.campa: The University of Mons, in the Belgian Borinage, confers an honorary doctorate on him. Europe honors him first, and this is not an accident: the continent's studios, from IRCAM outward, have been running his software for two decades, and the pieces written on it are in the touring repertoire of ensembles that never think to ask who wrote the patcher. He crosses the Atlantic to accept a degree from a university in coal country, a short train ride from the building where the first version ran. The date is the eleventh of May.
suggested_refs: Universite de Mons, honorary doctorates conferred 2011

stops.name: La Jolla, the center closes into Calit2
stops.date_confidence: attested to the day (Wikipedia, 'Center for Research in Computing and the Arts')
stops.campa: The Center for Research in Computing and the Arts ceases operations on the first of July, forty years after Roger Reynolds founded it as the Center for Music Experiment. Its functions, its support, and its facilities are folded into Calit2, the larger institute on the same campus. Puckette has been out of the associate directorship for a year and stays on the music faculty. The equipment he used goes up the hill without him, and the name comes off the door.
suggested_refs: Calit2 at UC San Diego, recipient of CRCA's functions and facilities in 2012
sources: Wikipedia, 'Center for Research in Computing and the Arts'

stops.name: Newton St Loe, the honorary degree at Bath Spa
stops.date_confidence: attested to the day (Wikipedia, 'Miller Puckette'); the ceremony is placed at the university's Newton Park campus, its principal site
stops.campa: Three weeks after the center in La Jolla closes, Bath Spa University gives him an honorary degree at its Newton Park campus, a country estate outside Bath proper in the parish of Newton St Loe, where the university's buildings stand in an eighteenth-century landscaped park with a lake and a ruined castle keep. Britain's electronic music courses teach Pd as standard, and the degree is given for that rather than for the medals or the mathematics. He accepts it in academic dress, in an English July, on the twenty-first.
suggested_refs: Bath Spa University honorary graduates, 2012
Newton Park, Newton St Loe, Somerset

stops.name: La Jolla, the two lineages at thirty years
stops.date_confidence: attested to the day (Wikipedia, 'Max (software)'). Pinned at Puckette's campus rather than at Ableton's Berlin offices or Cycling '74's, since he was party to neither transaction
stops.campa: Ableton, the Berlin company behind Live, announces on the sixth of June that it has acquired Cycling '74. Max keeps its name, its leadership, and its own publication, and is now owned by one of the largest software houses in music. Pd, on the same day, is a BSD-licensed source tree that anyone may fork, maintained from a university server by the man who started both lines. Thirty years after The Patcher, one branch has been bought and the other cannot be.
stops.quote: Despite its lightweight and portable nature, Pd offers a wide range of external packages that enhance its capabilities, primarily focusing on audio and control processing, but also for graphical processing and whatnot.
stops.quote_source: Pd Documentation, Chapter 2 (Theory of Operation), section 2.1 Overview, doc/1.manual/2.theory.of.operation.htm

stops.name: La Jolla, professor emeritus of computer music
stops.date_confidence: reconstruction: the emeritus title is attested (Wikipedia, 'Miller Puckette') but no date is given for it in any source reached, and UCSD's own pages could not be loaded (TLS certificate failure at msp.ucsd.edu). The year is a placement, not a claim
stops.campa: He becomes professor emeritus of computer music at the University of California, San Diego. The title ends the teaching obligation and none of the work: releases keep coming from his own server, the mailing lists keep filling, and bug reports keep arriving from Berlin and Belo Horizonte and Seoul. Installation artists and game-audio designers have built careers on what he wrote without ever taking a class from him. The releases go out as source, the way they have since 1996.
stops.quote: Pd is commonly used for live music performance, VeeJaying, sound effects, composition, audio analysis, interfacing with sensors, using cameras, controlling robots, designing apps, procedural audio for games or even interacting with websites.
stops.quote_source: Pd Documentation, Chapter 1 (Introduction), doc/1.manual/1.introduction.htm, pure-data/pure-data source repository

stops.name: Venice, the Silver Lion at the Arsenale
stops.date_confidence: award and year attested (Wikipedia, 'Miller Puckette'); labiennale.org confirms a ceremony at noon on 19 October 2023 but does not name the room. The venue is a reconstruction: Biennale Musica uses the Arsenale theatres (Teatro alle Tese, Teatro Piccolo Arsenale), not the Giardini, which is an art and architecture site
stops.campa: At noon on the nineteenth of October the Biennale awards him the Silver Lion in music. The ceremony belongs to the Arsenale, the republic's old shipyard, where Biennale Musica keeps its theatres among the brick sheds that once turned out a galley a day. The prize belongs to a state, and it is given to a programmer for a programming language, in a city that ran the first assembly line in Europe out of these same sheds. He is sixty-four. Manoury's Pluton is thirty-five years old and still performed on stages that no longer own a 4X.

stops.campa: Pure Data reaches version 0.56.5, packaged in Arch, in Debian, in Ubuntu, in the FreeBSD ports tree, still BSD-licensed, still shipped from his own university server rather than from a release page on a code-hosting site. Thirty years of point releases and a numbering scheme that has never reached 1.0 and shows no sign of intending to. What began as a drawing under the Place Igor-Stravinsky is now maintained by strangers on six continents. The platform list gives macOS, Windows and Linux, and then, still, ports for FreeBSD and IRIX.
